newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks finish steadier in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks finish steadier in listless trade.

text.p: South African shares ended Monday's trade steadier with industrials softening after early gains on the back of Friday's stronger Wall Street and golds heeding bullion's slight recoveries, dealers said.
They said the market's sentiment was cautious to bullish, but market players awaited cues from some of this week's economic indicators due for release.
Indicators due out are March consumer price and March trade figures on Wednesday and March M3 money supply and private credit growth on Thursday.

The industrial shares perked up sligthly early on Monday following Wall Street's Friday's gains, but softened in the afternoon with dealers saying market players saw New York's correction as not yet over.
The industrial index closed 22.5 points up at 8,338, the all-share ended up 17.8 points to 7,040 and the gold index gained 9.9 points to finish at 1,257.6.

Dealers said volumes had been moderate with 650 million rand worth of shares traded, while the bourse's financial index reached a new all time high of 8,695 compared with a previous record of 8,678 on March 13.
Golds were firmer on the back of a sligthly recovered bullion price, but a firmer rand held back real advances, dealers said.
Bullion stood at around $342 an ounce on Monday after trading below $340 an ounce last week.
Near-dated stock futures also steadied towards close with industrial futures receiving slight cheers from Friday's close of Wall Street and golds taking note of bullion's steady climb.
The June industrial contract was at 8,145/53 from 8,180 settlement, all-share was at 6,500/10 from 6,519 and the golds contract were at 885/91 from 878.
